claims.explanation: Sirolimus (rapamycin) allosterically inhibits mTORC1, so selectivity is best explained by dependence on mTORC1-driven growth and survival signaling rather than by any single lineage. Tumors with upstream PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation (PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutation, or high mTORC1 output) should be sensitized, whereas intact negative feedback or compensatory survival signaling can protect. The virtual-cell signature (mTOR inhibitors as top matches, HMGCR/HMGCS1 suppression) supports on-pathway mTORC1 inhibition as the selective mechanism.

features.basis: PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT/mTORC1, increasing rapamycin dependence; enriched in killed lines (ZR751, 786O, HEC265)
Activating PI3K mutations drive mTORC1 signaling; seen in HGC27, KYSE510, SNU840, HEC265
Higher mTOR pathway output predicts greater mTORC1 inhibitor sensitivity
mTORC1 scaffold abundance reflects pathway dependence targeted by sirolimus
Increased AKT signaling upstream of mTORC1 sensitizes to rapamycin
Higher PI3K catalytic subunit expression increases mTORC1 pathway flux
Retained PTEN restrains PI3K/AKT/mTORC1, reducing dependence on mTORC1
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least affected (GSU, CL11, T3M4, IPC298), suggesting MAPK-driven mTORC1 independence
BRAF-mutant melanomas appear in both groups but several are resistant (LOXIMVI, UACC62, IGR37), suggesting MAPK bypass
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines HCC4006 and NCIH1648 are least affected, indicating receptor-tyrosine-kinase bypass of mTORC1
STK11/LKB1 loss can relieve AMPK restraint and alter mTORC1 inhibitor response; seen in resistant KALS1 and SNU840
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in several resistant lines (LOXIMVI, FTC133, KALS1)
